prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one coherent scene and moment, no panels or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Kit and Zoe have equal standing height. Include only characters needed by this exact scene, not every reference pose. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Where Does Daylight Go?; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: World Discovery classroom at early evening; first a view through the window, then a darkened tabletop demonstration. Kit keeps one flashlight fixed at screen left while Zoe rotates one blue-green ball in place at center.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One plain blue-green globe-like ball; One removable small red dot on its surface; One yellow flashlight held steadily by Kit
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and development stage required below.
Page 6. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): That is like night at Zoe’s home. Other places still face the Sun.
Required illustration: World Discovery classroom at early evening; first a view through the window, then a darkened tabletop demonstration. Kit keeps one flashlight fixed at screen left while Zoe rotates one blue-green ball in place at center. The model’s red dot sits on the dark side while the opposite hemisphere remains lit; children observe the two sides. Exact state: No second dot; both light and dark portions visible at once.
Exact current state: No second dot; both light and dark portions visible at once.
Do not add later events, duplicate props or a separate inset. No written title; the app renders live text.
Third reference locks the approved classroom layout, plain teal ball and yellow flashlight. Kit remains LEFT and Zoe RIGHT. No continents or stand on MODEL BALL, only ONE red sticker. Keep flashlight fixed at same position. Physical light: LEFT half of ball lit pale teal, RIGHT half dark teal; light beam comes from LEFT and ENDS on ball, never continues behind. The single red dot is CLEARLY ON RIGHT DARK HALF, away from central boundary but still visible on near-facing surface. NOT centered, NOT on bright left half.

visualReview.note: Direct inspection: dot on dark right half while left remains lit; children observe; flashlight position unchanged and beam ends on sphere.
visualReview.limits: Direct agent image/sequence inspection; not physical classroom observation.
